name: Burg Freundsberg
kurzbeschreibung: Stately Burg Freundsberg towers above Schwaz as the historic landmark of the Silver Region, featuring a museum, chapel, and restaurant.
beschreibung:
Overview

The stately fortress of Burg Freundsberg rises on a prominent castle hill at an elevation of 675 meters high above the historic silver-mining town of Schwaz in the Lower Inn Valley. Founded around 1150 by the Lords of Freundsberg, the ancestral seat looks back upon nearly nine centuries of history and stands as the visible landmark of the entire Silver Region Karwendel. During the heyday of Schwaz silver mining in the 15th and 16th centuries, Tyrolean sovereigns, including Archduke Sigmund the Wealthy and Emperor Maximilian I, acquired the castle and converted its defensive tower into a royal residence. Today, the five-story Romanesque-Gothic keep houses the Schwaz Town Museum, guiding guests through regional history from prehistory and medieval mining to traditional Tyrolean folk art.

Route & Requirements

Visitors can walk up to the castle from Schwaz town center via the scenic, sunny castle path in about 25 minutes, or drive up comfortably by car or local city bus directly to the castle parking lot. The walking trail follows asphalt lanes and woodland paths with moderate incline, requiring standard fitness and ordinary walking shoes. The castle courtyard, the chapel with its valuable late-Gothic frescoes, and the castle restaurant are level and accessible for wheelchairs. Museum rooms inside the historic residential tower span several floors linked by steep wooden stairs requiring good footing. At the top of the tower, an observation gallery rewards visitors with an expansive panoramic view over Schwaz, the Inn Valley, and the crags of the Karwendel Nature Park.

Visit & Arrival

The Museum of the City of Schwaz at Burg Freundsberg and the castle tavern are open from May to late October daily except Mondays from 10:00 to 17:00. The courtyard and chapel are freely accessible; museum admission is affordably priced for individuals and families. Drivers arrive via the A12 Inntal motorway (exit Schwaz) and follow signs up to the castle (free parking on site). By train, take ÖBB or S-Bahn services to Schwaz station, where local city bus route 2 travels directly up to the castle.

Tips

Following your museum visit, enjoy a refreshing drink and traditional Tyrolean cooking on the shaded garden terrace with sweeping town views. Combine your visit with a tour of the famous Schwaz Silver Mine down in the valley for an ideal day out.
preis: Courtyard and chapel free; Schwaz Town Museum adults approx. €6.00 (children discounted)
oeffnungszeiten: May to late October open daily except Mondays from 10:00 to 17:00
